questions.text: A student is classifying the traditional auxiliary disciplines associated with studying the Vedas. Which set contains only Vedangas?
options: Ayurveda, Dhanurveda, Gandharvaveda, Arthashastra
Shiksha, Vyakarana, Chandas, Nirukta, Kalpa, Jyotisha
Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda
Dharma, Artha, Kama, Moksha

questions.text: A question asks which Purushartha refers most directly to liberation from the cycle of rebirth. Which answer fits?
options: Artha
Kama
Moksha
Dharma

questions.text: Which pairing best matches a traditional knowledge area to its subject?
options: Jyotisha — calendrical and astronomical calculations
Chandas — metalworking
Vyakarana — town drainage
Kalpa — textile dye chemistry

questions.text: A researcher studies historic methods of collecting seasonal runoff and storing it for dry periods in Gujarat. Which syllabus area is the closest match?
options: Vedic school of philosophy
Sanskrit components of language
Traditional water management and rainwater harvesting
Ashramas and stages of life

questions.text: A student claims that because Sanskrit has a formal grammatical tradition, modern natural-language processing can be understood only through Sanskrit. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: The tradition is relevant to studying language structure, but it does not establish that NLP can only be done through Sanskrit
The claim follows because formal grammar and NLP are identical
The tradition has no relevance because historical language study cannot inform computation
Sanskrit grammar proves every modern language has identical syntax

questions.text: A calendar researcher wants to understand traditional time reckoning rather than ethical goals of life. Which combination is most directly relevant?
options: Purusharthas and Ashramas
Itihasa and Puranas only
Metallurgy and textile dyeing
Vedanga Jyotisha and historical measurement units

questions.text: A museum label says an ancient water structure proves that every modern irrigation method originated in the same region. Which revision is most historically responsible?
options: Keep the claim because a surviving structure establishes universal origin
Describe the structure and its documented context, and avoid claiming universal origin without comparative evidence
Remove all discussion of water management because historical evidence is never useful
Replace the claim with a statement that ancient and modern systems are identical

questions.text: A project compares historical textile dyeing, metalworking and architecture with modern engineering. Which method best avoids both dismissing historical knowledge and making unsupported claims?
options: Assume historical methods were always more sustainable than modern methods
Treat every traditional account as experimentally verified
Compare documented techniques, materials, context and outcomes, distinguishing evidence from interpretation
Evaluate only the modern products and ignore the historical context

questions.text: A student equates Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha with four identical synonyms for morality. What is the strongest correction?
options: They are distinct Purusharthas—ethical duty, material prosperity, desire/enjoyment and liberation—with related but non-identical meanings
They are four names for Jyotisha
They describe only the four Vedas
They are stages of technical metal production

questions.text: A report uses the existence of a traditional town-planning text as proof that every historic settlement followed it exactly. What is the key flaw?
options: Texts cannot ever provide historical evidence
Architecture is unrelated to knowledge systems
Town planning can be studied only through modern maps
A prescriptive text does not by itself prove universal implementation; compare it with site-specific archaeological and historical evidence
